hero.subheadline: Icon buttons, chips, progress, an accordion, a table, a dialog and a menu: the building blocks a page is made of besides its words and pictures.
hero.headline: More blocks

data.headline: Actions, choices and waiting
data.intro: An icon button and a chip are things to press. Progress says that something is under way. Each is plain markup, drawn with Material’s values.
data.iconButtonNote: A button that holds an icon and no words: standard, filled, tonal and outlined, and each disabled. Every one has a name for assistive technology.
data.assistNote: An assist chip does one thing when it is pressed. It can hold an icon before its words.
data.filterNote: A filter chip is on or off, and several of a set can be on. It is the browser’s own checkbox, drawn as a chip.
data.progressNote: How far along something is, as a line or as a ring. With a number it shows how much is done; with none it shows only that it is at work.

data.headline: Questions and menus
data.intro: A dialog asks a question that must be answered before going on. A menu is a list of things to press that opens from a button. Each is the browser’s own, drawn with Material’s values.
data.dialogNote: It opens over the page, keeps the keyboard inside it, and closes on an answer, on a press outside it and on Escape. The view that asks is told the answer.

asks.label: Ask a question
asks.headline: Clear the list?
asks.text: Everything on the list is taken off it. This cannot be undone.

asks.label: Say one thing
asks.text: Your place is held for ten minutes.

answers.confirm: The answer was the confirming one.

data.menuNote: It opens beside its button and closes on a choice, on a press outside it and on Escape. Tab reaches its items. One menu here chooses among three; the other holds things to do, with an icon each.

items.a: A list whose rows open. Each row is the browser’s own details element, so it opens to a press, to Enter and to Space.

items.q: How does a page ask for it?
items.a: By drawing a list of questions and answers with the template faq-accordion.tmpl.html. The same data drawn with faq.tmpl.html shows every answer open.

items.q: Can more than one row be open?
items.a: Yes. Each row opens and closes by itself.

hero.subheadline: The five Material 3 button styles, in five sizes and two shapes, on button and link elements.
hero.headline: Buttons

data.headline: Button styles
data.intro: Each row shows one style: a button, a button with a leading icon, a disabled button, and the same three as links.

styles.name: Filled
styles.note: The highest emphasis. The class btn-primary renders the same.
styles.label: Button

styles.name: Tonal
styles.note: A middle ground between filled and outlined.
styles.label: Button

styles.name: Outlined
styles.note: Medium emphasis, for actions that are important but not primary.
styles.label: Button

styles.name: Elevated
styles.note: A tonal button with a shadow, for when the button needs lifting off a patterned surface.
styles.label: Button

styles.name: Text
styles.note: The lowest emphasis, for the least prominent actions.
styles.label: Button

data.sizesIntro: Each row shows one size: round filled, round tonal with an icon, square outlined, square elevated with an icon, disabled, and a text link.

sizes.name: Small, 40px
sizes.note: The class btn-sm. A button with no size class is this size.

hero.subheadline: Material’s form controls: the checkbox, the radio button, the switch, the slider, the select and the two text fields, alone and in a form.
hero.headline: Forms

data.headline: Form controls
data.intro: Each is the browser’s own control, drawn with Material’s values. Every one here can be pressed, and reached and worked with the keyboard.
data.checkboxNote: One or more of several, or one thing on or off. It is the browser’s own checkbox.
data.radioNote: One of several. Radio buttons of one name are one choice, and the arrow keys move between them.
data.radioErrorLabel: A choice that must be made
data.radioDisabledLabel: A choice that cannot be changed
data.switchNote: One thing on or off, at once. It is the browser’s own checkbox, given the switch role.
data.switchTrailing: At the end of a row, as a setting has it
data.sliderNote: A place along a range. It is the browser’s own range input: the arrow keys move it, and a finger drags it.
data.filledNote: The second of Material’s two text fields. Fields are filled where what holds them has the class fields-filled; everywhere else they are outlined.
data.filledSupport: An icon at its start, and supporting text under it.
